brief.name: Let the Scent Lead
brief.objective: Present LAVISH OUD in a calm, ingredient-inspired 15-second editorial video.
brief.audience: Illustrative GCC fragrance audience interested in oud-themed storytelling; not a measured audience.
brief.concept: An abstract approach to oud, spices and floral description, resolved into a precise product hero and CTA.
brief.tone: Intimate, restrained, contemporary, culturally careful; no claims of origin or inherited craftsmanship.
brief.keyMessage: A sensory introduction to LAVISH OUD based on the limited official description.

insights: The synthetic sample permits a concept study of ingredient-led oud storytelling, not a claim that this theme is currently trending.
LAVISH OUD official description mentions oud, spices and floral facets, which is sufficient for a sensory editorial structure.
Origin, artisanal production method, heritage endorsement, longevity and cultural authenticity claims are out of scope without proof.
analysis.rationale: LAVISH OUD is an actual verified product. The official description provides enough high-level vocabulary to structure a restrained four-scene visual progression: oud, spice/floral contrast, bottle, brand.
analysis.recommendation: Tell a concise sensorial story grounded only in the official LAVISH OUD description; invite exploration without cultural or performance claims.
assumptions: An oud-led sensory visual could interest a conceptual GCC fragrance audience.
Abstract warm gradients and typographic forms can carry sensory associations without invented product photography.
The campaign is a creative sketch rather than a validated brand history.
uncertainties: No real engagement series or current platform signals have been gathered.
Oud source, extraction process, dates and cultural credentials are not verified.
Arabic wording and sensory nuance need native/brand review.
MP4/poster are pending and frame-rate is a target, not observed.
